body.statement: For every selector construction, the equations of \(\mathcal M_R\), \(\sigma_s\), and \(\mathcal M_{H,s}\) imply, without additional assumptions, that \(C_{\sigma_s}=C\), \(X_{\sigma_s}=g_s(C,S)\), and the following surgical response rule holds for every \(J\subseteq\{C,X,Y\}\): if \(Y\in J\), then \(Y_j=j_Y\); if \(Y\notin J\), then \(Y_j=B_{C_j,X_j}\). In particular, response modularity is an immediate consequence of equation replacement on every branch on which the \(Y\)-equation has not itself been replaced.
body.justification: This lemma separates genuine selector restrictions from invariances already forced by the structural equations and intervention surgery.
body.gap: The content is an internal semantic audit of the constructed SCM rather than an additional maintained condition.
body.consumer: The projection theorem can invoke the structural branches without assuming its conclusion.
